ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle BAC=130^\circ$, the perpendicular bisectors of $AB$ and $AC$ intersect $BC$ at points $E$ and $F$, and intersect $AB$ and $AC$ at points $D$ and $G$, respectively. What is the measure of $\angle EAF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} \\
Since DE bisects AB perpendicularly, and FG bisects AC perpendicularly, \\
it follows that EB=EA, and FA=FC, \\
thus, $\angle$BAE=$\angle$B, $\angle$FAC=$\angle$C, \\
Since in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle$BAC=$130^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle$B+$\angle$C=$50^\circ$, \\
thus, $\angle$BAE+$\angle$FAC=$50^\circ$, \\
therefore, $\angle$EAF=$\angle$BAC−($\angle$BAE+$\angle$FAC)=$\boxed{80^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle ABC with vertex A near the bottom, B at the upper left, and C at the right. Points E and F are marked on side BC. Point D is on AB, and point G is on AC. A line through D and E is drawn as the perpendicular bisector of AB, and a line through G and F is drawn as the perpendicular bisector of AC. Segments AE and AF are drawn, forming the angle EAF inside angle BAC. Reasoning: Let ∠ABC = B and ∠ACB = C. Since E lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB, EA = EB. Thus triangle ABE is isosceles, so ∠BAE = ∠ABE. Because E lies on BC, ray BE is along BC, hence ∠ABE = ∠ABC = B. Therefore ∠BAE = B. Similarly, since F lies on the perpendicular bisector of AC, FA = FC. Thus triangle AFC is isosceles, so ∠FAC = ∠ACF. Because F lies on BC, ray CF is along CB, hence ∠ACF = ∠ACB = C. Therefore ∠FAC = C. In triangle ABC, ∠BAC = 130°, so B + C = 180° − 130° = 50°. Therefore ∠EAF = ∠BAC − ∠BAE − ∠FAC = 130° − (B + C) = 130° − 50° = 80°.
